summary: refactor(novel): split roster/audit-enrollments/at-risk into fetch -> analyze -> render; fix at-risk tie-break ranking
reason: The novel cross-resource commands fused fetching, joining, ranking and rendering into single 103-148 line cobra RunE closures. The join and ranking rules — the reason these commands exist, since no single Canvas endpoint returns their output — had no interface to test through, so the generated per-command tests could only assert that --help renders and --dry-run returns nil. That test shape hid a live defect: at-risk broke ties between students on a string user ID, ranking user 10 above user 9. Each command now exposes a pure analyze function over already-fetched data, making the rules testable without a Canvas token, and the ranking bug is fixed.
validated_outcome: go test ./... green across all 6 packages; go vet and gofmt clean; roster, audit-enrollments and at-risk verified under --help and --dry-run --agent. 36 tests added, none requiring a Canvas token; each rule mutation-checked (12 mutations, 12 caught). golangci-lint was not available in the environment, so the lint gate is unverified.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Emit hand-authored transcendence commands as fetch -> analyze -> render rather than one RunE closure: a pure analyze(<command>Input) (<command>View, []map[string]any) alongside the existing shared fetch (canvasFetchList) and render (emitNovel) helpers.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Machine-level, not Canvas-specific. Every printed CLI's novel commands share this shape, so every one of them inherits the same untestable middle. The generated per-command smoke tests are stamped DO NOT EDIT and short-circuit at the dryRunOK guard, which is the first statement in RunE, so they cannot reach the join or ranking logic in any printed CLI. The durable fix is a template change plus a generated analyze-test stub that exercises the rule rather than the wiring; this local patch should be superseded by it.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: Generated novel-command test files should not be stamped DO NOT EDIT while inviting authors to fill in real cases.
deferred_to_upstream.reason: at_risk_test.go and its five siblings carry a DO NOT EDIT header alongside the comment 'Always runs — do not delete this test when filling in real cases', which asks for edits to a file a reprint overwrites. Real rule tests had to go in separate hand-authored files instead.
